transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Nassar (Redwood SE), Priya Sinha (Redwood CSM), Jorge Martinez (ArborHealth Procurement), Ava Chen (ArborHealth Legal), Marcus Reed (ArborHealth IT Sec), Nora Kim (ArborHealth Vendor Ops)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through the MSA / DPA ask list and pricing approval flow, quick intros?
[00:18] Jorge Martinez: Jorge Martinez, procurement at ArborHealth. We'll probably coordinate the PO timing and approvals.
[00:23] Ava Chen: Ava Chen, legal. I'll be reviewing the DPA and any proposed exceptions.
[00:28] Marcus Reed: Marcus Reed, security. I'll validate the SOC and KMS details plus any network requirements.
[00:34] Lena Park: Great. From Redwood, Omar our solutions engineer will walk through architecture constraints for PHI and dedicated options, and Priya will help with pricing and onboarding timeline.
[00:44] Omar Nassar: Hi all. Quick note up front - we support Hosted API for fastest time-to-value and Redwood Dedicated for isolated GPU pools, VPC peering, and optional on-prem. For PHI we typically recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and restricted egress; that said we can also support a VPC-hosted private control plane.
[01:10] Marcus Reed: When you say KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys or only cloud KMS? Our policy prefers HSM for key custody.
[01:20] Omar Nassar: Currently we integrate with major cloud KMS providers and have HSM-backed options via partner integrations; we can provide the integration diagram and evidence. We'll include the KMS note in the packet.
[01:37] Ava Chen: On the DPA, our legal team will likely ask to limit subprocessors and have strict data retention windows. We need clarity on logs - what you retain and for how long.
[01:47] Lena Park: Understood. On the DPA one-pager we'll call out retention defaults and options for shorter retention or customer-managed logs. Also audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[02:05] Nora Kim: Procurement question - what's the typical lead time between signing the MSA and Redwood enabling Dedicated capacity? We need that to plan go-live and budget cycles.
[02:15] Priya Sinha: Typical is 2-6 weeks depending on GPU capacity and region; for reserved Dedicated with a purchase order it's usually 2-4 weeks if no custom network setup. If it's on-prem that adds more time.
[02:31] Jorge Martinez: For our internal approvals we need a clear pricing worksheet and the monthly vs usage tradeoffs. Can you provide a line-item breakdown for pilot vs full production?
[02:43] Priya Sinha: Yes, we'll send an itemized pricing matrix showing per-token hosted costs, committed reserved capacity monthly fees, and estimated unit economics at different throughput bands. We'll also include a pilot discount row.
[02:58] Ava Chen: On SLAs, can you confirm remediation steps for downtime? We rarely accept just credit-based remedies; we need escalation path and a named contact.
[03:10] Lena Park: We can provide SLA language with uptime targets and guaranteed response times for Sev1 incidents; Redwood includes an escalation ladder and named contacts for enterprise contracts. We'll surface that in the MSA redline.
[03:28] Marcus Reed: How granular are your latency SLOs? Our clinical workflows need sub-200ms median for scoring models in the critical path.
[03:38] Omar Nassar: Sub-200ms median is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernels and local GPUs; we'll share latency benchmarks for similar model families and profile guidance (sequence lengths, batching). Note: batching can improve throughput but will affect p95 latency.
[03:58] Ava Chen: A lot of the DPA text references subprocessors. Are your model catalog partners considered subprocessors? For example, if you route to a different model provider in a fallback.
[04:12] Lena Park: Good call. We'll clarify subprocessors and fallback behaviors — we can explicitly list model variants and the policy that prevents cross-account data leakage.
[04:25] Jorge Martinez: Regarding procurement, does Redwood require net-30 or net-60? And do you accept standard vendor onboarding forms?
[04:35] Priya Sinha: Typically we accept net-30; net-60 can be considered on larger agreements. We can fill out vendor onboarding forms but will need a PO to attach to the contract for Dedicated capacity.
[04:47] Marcus Reed: Security artifacts - we need SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summaries, and ideally architecture diagrams that show egress controls.
[04:58] Omar Nassar: We'll upload SOC 2 extracts and a redacted pen test summary; architecture diagrams including VPC peering, security groups, and egress filter options. Also note that KV cache is in-memory and not persisted unless customers enable logging — I'll clarify that in writing. (quick aside: sometimes transcript shows kay-vee cache)
[05:20] Ava Chen: For the DPA, any limits on data residency? We are bound to keep data in-region for some subsets.
[05:28] Lena Park: We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private; Hosted API can be regionally routed but isn’t guaranteed unless we provision a region-specific instance. We'll call this out.
[05:40] Nora Kim: Any pre-approved security exceptions you typically accept? E.g., MFA for service accounts vs SSO requirements.
[05:48] Marcus Reed: Also, SAML vs OIDC - our identity team prefers SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[05:55] Omar Nassar: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; service accounts can be gated by MFA policies. We'll include a short compatibility matrix.
[06:08] Jorge Martinez: On pricing approvals, what's the best way to get expedited approval? Do you have a standard procurement packet?
[06:15] Priya Sinha: Yes - we'll prepare a procurement packet: one-page commercial summary, itemized pricing matrix, pilot proposal, and acceptance criteria for handoff. That usually expedites legal and procurement review.
[06:28] Ava Chen: If we need to add a DPA amendment for PHI, how do you handle that?
[06:34] Lena Park: We can provide a PHI addendum template; for Dedicated we can support PHI under an addendum with appropriate security controls and KMS options. We'll confirm specifics in the redline.
[06:45] Marcus Reed: About audit logs: how long do logs persist and how are they accessed? We need syslog forwarding for long-term retention.
[06:52] Omar Nassar: For Dedicated we can stream audit logs to a customer's logging endpoint (syslog/S3) and set retention policies. Defaults are 30 days in our control plane unless the customer pulls them or configures forwarding.
[07:10] Jorge Martinez: Any standard penalties if SLA isn't met other than credits? Our procurement prefers defined remediation checkpoints.
[07:18] Lena Park: We can add a two-tier remediation: credits plus mandatory root-cause review within X days and an escalation to commercial teams if outages persist. We'll propose language.
[07:32] Ava Chen: Are you open to redline on indemnity and liability caps? Those tend to be negotiation points.
[07:40] Lena Park: Yes, standard negotiation. We typically propose a liability cap based on fees paid in the prior 12 months; we can discuss exceptions for willful misconduct.
[07:53] Marcus Reed: A technical question - do you support private endpoints for inference so model calls don't traverse public internet?
[07:59] Omar Nassar: Yes, Dedicated supports private endpoints via VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud; on-prem also available for fully air-gapped. We'll include a diagram.
[08:12] (pause)
[08:20] Ava Chen: Will you be sharing a proposed MSA redline or do you expect us to start with your template?
[08:26] Lena Park: We'll send our standard MSA with redlines called out where common legal asks are typically accepted; if you prefer to start from your form we can review that too but it slows process. We recommend using our template to move faster.
[08:39] Jorge Martinez: Timeline wise - if we get the redline by 5/21 and our procurement team takes 5-7 business days, we could be in a PO stage by early June. Is that realistic?
[08:51] Priya Sinha: That sounds realistic given no major redlines and capacity available.
[08:58] Nora Kim: For the pilot, do you require data residency or is sample anonymized data fine?
[09:05] Omar Nassar: Sample anonymized data is fine for initial functional pilot; for end-to-end PHI testing we'd recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.
[09:18] Ava Chen: A few DPA specifics: deletion upon contract termination, right to audit, subprocessors list - we'll need those in a single page summary.
[09:27] Lena Park: Agreed - we'll produce a DPA summary table with deletions, subprocessors, retention, and audit rights.
[09:35] Jorge Martinez: Any special approval needed for government customers? We sometimes have FedRAMP considerations.
[09:42] Omar Nassar: We don't currently hold FedRAMP; for highly regulated workloads we recommend Private on-prem or dedicated region deployments with additional compliance controls. We'll note that.
[09:53] (transcription glitch: speaker labeled as Speaker 2 chuckles)
[10:03] Marcus Reed: Regarding fallback model routing - if Redwood falls back to a different provider for capacity, does that trigger data flow to a third party? Our DPA tightness will require explicit approval.
[10:16] Lena Park: We'll add explicit fallback policy: no cross-tenant data sharing; fallback only to vetted provider model variants and we will list those providers. If fallback behavior would move data off-cloud we will require customer pre-approval.
[10:30] Jorge Martinez: For procurement paperwork - do you accept electronic signatures and e-docs?
[10:36] Priya Sinha: Yes, e-signature is fine; we also support manual PO attachment.
[10:42] Ava Chen: On limiting subprocessors, are you able to provide a current subprocessor registry?
[10:48] Lena Park: Yes, we'll provide a subprocessor registry export and the DPA will include notification windows for new subprocessors.
[10:58] Nora Kim: For onboarding, is there a standard onboarding checklist we fill out?
[11:05] Priya Sinha: We'll send an onboarding checklist that covers account setup, VPC peering, SSO, SAML config, KMS setup, and production readiness tests.
[11:16] Marcus Reed: One more on security: do you allow customer-controlled encryption for data at rest within inference caches?
[11:24] Omar Nassar: For Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys and at-rest encryption; in-memory KV cache can't be encrypted at rest when in active GPU memory, but persistence layers can be encrypted. We'll be explicit about that nuance.
[11:45] Lena Park: Ok, circling back to deliverables - we're committing to share redline, DPA one-pager, SOC 2 extract, architecture diagram, and pricing matrix by 5/21. Anything else from ArborHealth side?
[11:58] Jorge Martinez: We'll route the vendor packet internally and send the PO timeline. Also we'll return the vendor risk questionnaire.
[12:06] Ava Chen: We'll return legal comments, likely with a few markups around subprocessors and liability caps.
[12:13] Nora Kim: I'll take action to coordinate procurement privacy team and share the vendor intake form.
[12:20] (background cross-talk)
[12:30] Lena Park: Awesome. Any blocker that would stop us from circling back with the documents?
[12:35] Jorge Martinez: Not at the moment.
[12:38] Ava Chen: No blockers, thanks.
[12:41] Marcus Reed: No blockers.
[12:43] Lena Park: Great. We'll follow up with the packet. One more quick note — pricing approvals: if procurement needs a formal quote to route, we'll provide a signed quote template.
[12:55] Priya Sinha: We'll also include an estimated cost model for expected token volumes so your finance folks can plug numbers in.
[13:05] Lena Park: Okay let's capture next steps.

[13:10] -- End of recorded transcript --

ArborHealth to complete vendor questionnaire and route the packet through procurement and legal. Action items documented.
